ECEA 5370 Network Systems Foundations

Instructor: Eric Keller

Course Description

Welcome! Throughout this course, Network Systems Foundations, you will delve into the fundamental layers of network communication. You will start with a thorough discussion of the Link Layer and its crucial role, moving on to the intricacies of Internet Protocol (IP) and router data planes, and then navigate through the complexities of the transport layer, application layer, and network security. With a practical focus, you'll write Python code to manage routing tables, analyze network traffic, simulate router functionalities, and create digital certificates for web servers. By the end of this course, you will have a well-rounded understanding of networking principles, from data transmission and routing to application protocols and security, and will be equipped with practical skills to navigate the ever-evolving landscape of network technology.

Drops, Tuition Refunds, and Withdrawals

Because the MS-ECE has flexible course start dates, all drops, tuition refunds, withdrawals, and grades are handled at the individual course level. It is the student’s responsibility to monitor these deadlines. Coursera and CU Boulder are not responsible for notifying the students of these deadlines. You can drop or withdraw from a course via Your Programs & Enrollment Card via BuffPortal.

Drops and Refunds

Each student has 14 days from a class start date or their enrollment date (whichever is later) to drop for 100% tuition refund. Students are only eligible to drop a course if they have not accessed the restricted content (final exam or project). When a course is dropped under these conditions, it will not appear on the student’s record.

Students who access the final exam or project are assigned a grade and ineligible for a drop, withdrawal, or refund.

Withdrawal

Students may withdraw from a course after the 14-day period only if they have not accessed restricted content (final exam or project). In such cases, the course will not be eligible for a refund. When a student withdraws or does not complete the restricted content (final exam or project), a grade of "W" will be recorded on their academic transcript. This "W" grade does not impact the student's GPA or total earned credits.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Guidance

Conditional AI Tool Usage: You may use AI tools for all assignments. You must critically evaluate and modify any AI-generated content, and disclose and document your usage per the AI Usage Documentation Best Practices below.

AI Usage Documentation Best Practices

When using AI tools in your academic work, it is essential to accurately document how and why you used them. AI tools should be considered as aids rather than primary sources. Therefore, remember to:

  • Reference AI assistance. In your references or bibliography section, mention the AI tool used and the nature of its contribution. For example: "Assistance provided by [AI Tool Name] for generating initial content ideas, response to [prompt], [month, day, year]”.

  • Document your process. Save screenshots, dialog, prompt, queries or version history to document your process if you used AI. Include documentation in the submission if the assignment format allows. Otherwise, save it in your system in case you are asked by a program or university staff.

Suspected Violations of this Policy

If program staff suspects you may have used AI tools to complete assignments in ways not explicitly authorized or suspect other violations of the honor code, they will contact you via email. Be sure to respond promptly to any related communication so your perspective is included in the case review. Failure to respond timely will not prevent the completion of a case review.

Turnitin and similar AI detection tools may be used in these courses for initial detection of possible honor code violations. All suspected violations will be reviewed by a human. AI tools alone will not be used to determine if an assignment is plagiarized, and results from these tools will not be used alone as evidence to penalize students.

University Policies

Accommodation for Disabilities

If you qualify for accommodations because of a disability, please submit your accommodation letter to your program at msece-accomodations@colorado.edu in a timely manner so that your needs can be addressed. Disability Services determines accommodations based on documented disabilities in the academic environment. Information on requesting accommodations is located on the Disability Services website. Contact Disability Services at 303-492-8671 or dsinfo@colorado.edu for further assistance. If you have a temporary medical condition or injury, see Temporary Medical Conditions under the Students tab on the Disability Services website.

Classroom Behavior

Students and faculty each have responsibility for maintaining an appropriate learning environment. Those who fail to adhere to such behavioral standards may be subject to discipline. Professional courtesy and sensitivity are especially important with respect to individuals and topics dealing with race, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy, age, disability, creed, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, political affiliation or political philosophy. Class rosters are provided to the instructor with the student's legal name. We will gladly honor your request to address you by an alternate name or gender pronoun. Please advise us of this preference early in the semester so that we may make appropriate changes to my records. For more information, see the Student Code of Conduct.

Honor Code

The University of Colorado Boulder takes issues of academic dishonesty extremely seriously. 

Students in all of CU Boulder’s courses, whether not-for-credit or for-credit, are expected to perform to the highest standards of academic honesty. 

Students enrolled in for-credit courses are members of the CU Boulder’s community and are subject to the Honor Code Office’s policies and procedures. Information on the Honor Code can be found at the Honor Code Office website.

Students who violate the Honor Code are subject to discipline. Violations of the policy may include: plagiarism, cheating, fabrication, lying, bribery, threats, unauthorized access to academic materials, submitting the same or similar work in more than one course without permission from all course instructors involved, and aiding academic dishonesty. Students are specifically expected to turn in original work and cite portions created by other authors. If a student has doubts regarding what collaboration is permissible in the course, the student should consult the discussion forums or the course facilitator directly.

Violations also include facilitating any act which may help a student to gain an unfair academic advantage including:

  1. Sharing course materials, including but not limited to personal notes, in an unauthorized online bank or forum, whether for profit or for free, is strongly discouraged and may result in a referral to the Honor Code. This includes sharing course materials on Slack.

  2. Sharing personal authentication credentials/login information to third party sites is strongly discouraged and may result in a referral to the Honor Code process

Sexual Misconduct, Discrimination, Harassment and/or Related Retaliation

The University of Colorado Boulder (CU Boulder) is committed to fostering a positive and welcoming learning, working, and living environment. CU Boulder will not tolerate acts of sexual misconduct, intimate partner abuse (including dating or domestic violence), stalking, or protected-class discrimination or harassment by members of our community. Individuals who believe they have been subject to misconduct or retaliatory actions for reporting a concern should contact the Office of Institutional Equity and Compliance (OIEC) at 303-492-2127 or cureport@colorado.edu. Information about the OIEC, university policies, anonymous reporting, and the campus resources can be found on the OIEC website. 

Please know that faculty and instructors have a responsibility to inform OIEC when made aware of incidents of sexual misconduct, discrimination, harassment and/or related retaliation, to ensure that individuals impacted receive information about options for reporting and support resources.

Religious Holidays

Campus policy regarding religious observances requires that faculty make every effort to deal reasonably and fairly with all students who, because of religious obligations, have conflicts with scheduled exams, assignments or required attendance. Since this is an online class, with no fixed weekly calendar schedule, we ask that you arrange your workload to accommodate your religious practice. See the campus policy regarding religious observances for full details.

Auto-graded Assessments

As you complete any auto-graded assessment, please consider the following:

  • Some assessments may include a set of instructions with a list of resources you are and aren't to use. While these assessments may not be proctored, please consider adhering to this list of resources as the assessment was designed with the list in mind.

  • Most auto-graded assessments will allow for multiple attempts. Between attempts, it is recommended you review feedback provided for correct and incorrect responses and relevant course materials before starting your next attempt.

  • Some programming assignments will contain hidden test cases that are graded. If you do not receive full credit for your submission, please review your assignment summary for the passed and failed tests so you can further optimize your solutions.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Usage Guidance

Artificial intelligence tools—software that reproduces text, images, computer code, audio, video, and other content—have become widely available. Well-known examples include ChatGPT for text and DALL•E for images. This statement governs all such tools, including those released during your enrolled session. 

It is your responsibility—not the tool’s—to assure the quality, integrity, and accuracy of work you submit in all CU Boulder courses. Keep in mind that AI tools are designed to create content that seems to have been produced by a human, not to produce accurate or reliable content; therefore, relying on an AI tool may result in inaccurate content. Be wary of unintentional plagiarism or data fabrication. Act with integrity, for the sake of both your personal character and your academic record.

Consider the impact of using AI tools on your learning goals: in most cases, using an AI-generated answer without critical review and significant input from your end is contrary to the overall goal of personal learning and development in your chosen area. 

Respect copyright and privacy. You may only enter your own data into AI tools. Do not enter private, sensitive, or copyrighted data from others into AI tools without their consent. Avoid using AI for purposes that are private, sensitive, or high-risk.

Consider your environmental impact. Using AI models requires large amounts of electricity, water, and rare earth minerals. When using AI, keep in mind there are environmental concerns associated with its use.

For assessments that allow Conditional AI Usage

You may use AI tools on these assessments. However, you must critically evaluate and modify any AI-generated content, and disclose and document your usage per the AI Usage Documentation Guidelines below.

You CAN use AI tools to...

  • Supplement your understanding of course material (e.g., summarizing a PDF that you have read to ensure comprehension)

  • Generate practice questions for assignments, quizzes, and tests

  • Check your spelling and grammar

  • Translate course materials or your own work

  • Act as a tutor to identify and explain weaknesses in your draft answers

  • Ask AI to help you debug your code.

  • Generate project ideas, outlines, and help with brainstorming

  • Edit answers that you have written yourself, but not create additional content or ideas

You CANNOT use AI tools to...

  • Submit exact or similar/paraphrased assignment questions or prompts into the AI tool

  • Edit your submission in other ways not listed in the allowable examples above

  • Generate partial or entire answers for graded assignments in place of your own work or thinking

  • Help with a graded assignment in any way without attaching documentation of that usage (see AI Usage Documentation Guidelines below)

AI Usage Documentation Best Practices

When using AI tools in your academic work, it is essential to accurately document how and why you used them. AI tools should be considered as aids rather than primary sources. Therefore, remember to:

  • Reference AI assistance. In your references or bibliography section, mention the AI tool used and the nature of its contribution. For example: "Assistance provided by [AI Tool Name] for generating initial content ideas, response to [prompt], [month, day, year]”.

  • Document your process. Save screenshots, dialog, prompt, queries or version history to document your process if you used AI. Include documentation in the submission if the assignment format allows. Otherwise, save it in your system in case you are asked by a program or university staff.  

Assessments and Academic Honesty

As you complete assessments, you are expected to perform to the highest standards of academic honesty. Please keep the following in mind:

  • Copying the provided rubrics to use as your own work is considered plagiarism.

  • Copying your peers work that you have reviewed in peer review assignments is considered plagiarism.

  • Using generative AI services, such as ChatGPT, to write your peer review assignments or answer other graded assignment questions and submitting those as your own work is considered plagiarism.

  • Using question-and-answer websites, such as Stack Overflow or Chegg, to post assessment questions and solicit solutions and then submitting responses as your own work is considered plagiarism.

These slides are used for all of the lessons in Week 1.

nf-01-link-slides-UPDATE-2025-07-02.pdf

Which of these is a valid Ethernet MAC address

  • 20:f1:9e:bd:3b:18

  • FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF

  • 2001:db8:85a3:8d3:1319:8a2e:370:7348

  • 10.10.2.10

Which of these is not a field in the Ethernet header

  • Quality of Service (QoS)

  • Destination (dst)

  • Source (src)

  • Type

For even parity, what would be the parity bit for this data: 0101 0001

Indicate which of the following is a characteristic of the Ethernet FCS field

  • Can detect a single bit error

  • Can detect burst errors

  • Can be calculated as the data is arriving off of the wire

  • Is used to determine vendor of the network card

  • Can fix any single bit error

Which is a negative property of channel partitioning (e.g., time or frequency division multiplexing)?

  • The channel isn’t efficiently used unless all nodes have data to send

  • Collisions occur frequently

  • A sender can become blocked from being able to transmit its data

  • It requires complex coordination with an arbiter

In CSMA / CD, how does a node detect whether the transmission encountered a collision or not?

  • The protocol ensures collisions cannot occur

  • It will simultaneously read from the channel while transmitting, and compare the read and sent values – if different, a collision occurred

  • The receiver will send an ACK back to the sender indicating it successfully received the message

In CSMA / CA, how does a node detect whether the transmission encountered a collision or not?

  • The receiver will send an ACK back to the sender indicating it successfully received the message

  • It will simultaneously read from the channel while transmitting, and compare the read and sent values – if different, a collision occurred

  • The protocol ensures collisions cannot occur

Given a switch with MAC table with (20:30:40:50:60:70 – port 0), if it receives a frame with destination FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF, what will it do?

  • Forward out port 0

  • Drop

  • Forward out all ports

Given a switch with MAC table with (20:30:40:50:60:70 – port 0), if it receives a frame with destination 20:30:40:50:60:70, what will it do?

  • Forward out all ports

  • Drop

  • Forward out port 0

Given a switch with MAC table with (20:30:40:50:60:70 – port 0), if it receives a frame with destination 20:30:40:22:AA:22, what will it do?

  • Forward out all ports

  • Drop

  • Forward out port 0

These slides are used in all of the Week 2 lessons.

nf-02-network-slides-UPDATE-2025-07-02.pdf

We noted that IP prefixes can be aggregated. Which of the following are equivalent

  • Neither

  • (10.0.0.0/16, 10.1.0.0/16, 10.2.0.0/16, 10.3.0.0/16) and 10.0.0.0/14

  • (10.0.0.0/16, 10.1.0.0/16, 10.2.0.0/16, 10.3.0.0/16) and 10.0.0.0/18

What is the service model offered by the Internet Protocol

  • Best Effort

  • Reliable stream of in order packets

  • Guaranteed delivery of packets

Which of the following is a prefix for which 1.2.3.4 is covered by.

  • 1.0.0.0/24

  • 1.2.0.0/22

  • 1.2.4.0/24

  • 1.0.0.0/16

In the data plane, the destination IP address is looked up in what table?

  • Forwarding Table

  • MAC Learning Table

  • Routing Table

  • ARP Table

With IP forwarding, the entries in the forwarding table are prefixes. If two entries overlap (e.g., 11.11.11.0/24 and 11.11.0.0/16, for which 11.11.11.11 matches both), how is it determined which entry to use?

  • The oldest entry is preferred

  • The entry with the longest prefix is preferred

  • The newest entry is preferred

  • A round robin selector is used to rotate between them

For a switching fabric, what is a benefit of a cross bar over a bus?

  • It is standardized by the IETF

  • It uses thicker wires

  • It can support multiple packets being switched simultaneously

BGP (path vector) or OSPF (link state) or both? Knows entire topology.

  • BGP

  • OSPF

  • Both

BGP (path vector) or OSPF (link state) or both? Handles failure of devices.

  • BGP

  • OSPF

  • Both

BGP (path vector) or OSPF (link state) or both? May pick a different best route than its neighbor.

  • BGP

  • OSPF

  • Both

BGP (path vector) or OSPF (link state) or both? Is the main protocol used in the Internet.

  • BGP

  • OSPF

  • Both

BGP (path vector) or OSPF (link state) or both? Exchanges with neighbor all routes known.

  • BGP

  • OSPF

  • Both

BGP (path vector) or OSPF (link state) or both? Works in a decentralized manner.

  • BGP

  • OSPF

  • Both

Before an IP packet can be sent to a destination it needs to know the MAC address of the destination if on the same LAN or of the next hop router otherwise. What protocol can be used

  • DNS

  • ARP

  • TCP

  • DHCP

Which best describes how ping works

  • IP header specified ICMP as the protocol, and sends an ICMP request to the desired IP destination, who then responds with an ICMP reply.

  • Ethernet header specifies ICMP as the type, and routers will forward or respond based on the ICMP header.

  • Through a separate management channel, a link layer protocol, ICMP, is used.

  • An IP options field has a flag in it specifying this is a ping request

These slides are used in each of the lessons in Week 3.

nf-03-transport-slides.pdf

Which of the following best characterizes the main property of the network and transport layers in general that would be true for all protocols.

  • Network layer provides best effort, Transport layer provides error correction

  • Network layer provides addressing that is only locally unique, Transport layer provides addressing that is globally unique

  • Network layer uses numbers to represent addresses, Transport layer uses meaningful strings.

  • Network layer provides host to host communication, Transport provides process to process.

Which of the following is true:

  • Both UDP and TCP are connection oriented

  • UDP is connection oriented, TCP is connectionless

  • UDP is connectionless, TCP is connection oriented

  • Both UDP and TCP are connectionless

Which of the following could occur in an IP network that requires TCP to provide a mechanism for reliable communication? (select all that apply)

  • Error in the packet (bit flip)

  • An administrator may monitor the traffic

  • Congestion can occur in the switches/routers buffers

  • Different packets can take different paths (even to the same destination)

Which header fields in TCP are key to reliable communication?

  • RequestForRetransmit flag

  • BufferReservation flag, and Allocation request fields during setup

  • Congestion Control

  • Sequence number, and Acknowledgement number

Assume data is being transferred in one direction - from host A to host B, under which condition is flow control needed?

  • A can send at 100Gbps, B can receive at 1Gbps

  • A uses an Internet Service provider with only 10Mbps upload speed

  • B uses an Internet Service provider with only 10Mbps download speed

  • A can send at 1Gbps, B can receive at 100Gbps

What is congestion collapse?

  • Where applications fail due to packet loss from congestion in the network

  • Where the goodput of a network decreases when the offered load by hosts on the network increases past a certain point.

  • Where throughput gradually decreases the closer a link gets to full capacity

  • The point at which network devices (routers) explicitly signal to the sending host that it is congested.

In TCP’s congestion control, what are feedback signals it receives that congestion exists and it should reduce its sending rate? (select all that apply)

  • Timeout waiting for an acknowledgement

  • Receiving a duplicate acknowledgement

  • Receiving a datagram with an in-order sequence number

  • Receiving a datagram requesting to change port numbers

What does the congestion window in TCP control?

  • How much data is allowed to be in flight at one time.

  • The amount of time the sender should wait before sending more packets to wait for the network to become uncongested.

  • The time of day during which the network is typically congested and should be avoided

  • The rate at which the receiver delivers data to the application

These slides are used in each of the lessons in Week 4.

nf-04-application-slides.pdf

In DNS, how do DNS resolvers know about root servers?

  • The IP addresses are hard coded within the resolver’s code/configuration.

  • It uses ARP to query on its local area network.

  • The don’t – DNS resolvers don’t know about root servers, which are run as a trusted and private Internet service only available to ISPs.

  • It queries DNS with the fully qualified domain name of the root servers (a.root‑servers.net, b.root‑servers.net, etc.)

In DNS, what happens when a DNS server does not know the IP address of the domain in the query.

  • Responds with the name of another resolver that it knows as authoritative for part of the domain.

  • Hangs the server.

  • Responds with the IP address of the resolver.

  • Silently discards the request.

In sockets programming, which would be an appropriate sequence of functions called.

  • socket(), bind(), listen(), accept()

  • bind(), recv(), accept(), send()

  • bind(), send(), accept(), recv()

  • socket(), accept(), listen(), bind()

True or false: socket programming is limited to being used in the C/C++ language

  • True

  • False

Application protocol defines which of the following

  • Amount of buffering in the Transport stack.

  • Programming language of client and server

  • Message transmission time

  • Message syntax and semantics

For HTTP messages that use JSON, which of the following can be expressed (check all that apply).

  • arrays

  • strings

  • integers

  • objects

What role does the protobufs compiler play in the gRPC workflow.

  • It provides a language neutral acceleration library for client/server applications.

  • It performs validation of JSON messages.

  • It transforms JSON data formatted messages into a binary form.

  • It generates libraries in different languages that provides stubs for serializing and deserializing data that can be used by client and server software.

Which is the biggest distinguishing difference between JSON and Protobufs

  • JSON is an open standard, protobufs require a paid license from google to use.

  • JSON is textual, protobufs are binary.

  • JSON is popular, protobufs are not.

  • JSON is supported in many languages, protobufs are only supported in go and python.

These slides are used in each of the lessons in Week 5.

nf-05-netsec-slides.pdf

What are general negatives about symmetric and asymmetric encryption respectfully

  • Symmetric encryption requires shared secret keys, asymmetric encryption is slow.

  • Software is generally not available that can perform either symmetric or asymmetric encryption

  • Symmetric encryption is vulnerable to eavesdropping, asymmetric encryption requires parts of the message to be plaintext.

  • Symmetric encryption is slow, asymmetric encryption requires shared secret keys.

What mechanism of IPsec keeps the communications confidential?

  • Encryption

  • Hashing

  • Message Authentication Codes

  • Digital Certificates

What is the purpose of the Diffie Helman protocol as used in IPsec

  • Exchange security parameters

  • Ensure the network is performant enough for data exchange

  • Distribute a public key of a server

  • Exchange a shared symmetric key

What is an attack that can be performed that RPKI protects against

  • Man in the middle attacks

  • Route hijacking

  • Eavesdropping

  • Denial of Service

What entities serve as the main certificate authorities in RPKI

  • A government agency

  • Network vendors such as Cisco, Juniper, Palo Alto

  • Regional Internet Registries

  • Universities

What are three concerns with HTTP that HTTPS helps address

  • Traffic is in plaintext, data has no integrity protection, the TCP three way handshake is insecure

  • Data encoding, data size, and data fidelity

  • DNS requests are UDP, data is encoded inefficiently, APIs are openly accessible

  • Traffic is in plaintext, data has no integrity protection, client can’t be sure server is their intended communication partner.

What is a mechanism that Let’s Encrypt uses to validate the identity of a request for a signed digital certificate?

  • Let’s Encrypt accepts all requests as its only purpose is for testing https locally

  • The Let’s Encrypt team performs a background check on the requestor

  • An admin from Let’s Encrypt sets up a video call with the requestor

  • Admin places a token at a known address on their website, and if Let’s Encrypt is able to fetch it, it proves ownership.

The course final examination is similar in format to the other graded assignments, with the following characteristics:

  • The exam is unproctored.

  • The exam is two hours long.

  • The exam is 34 questions.

  • You are allowed 1 attempt.

    • An attempt is one complete try at the exam within the given time limit.

  • Each attempt allows 1 submission.

    • A submission occurs when you click “Submit” during an attempt.

  • After the attempt window has ended, you will not be able to change or re-take the exam.

  • The exam contains multiple-choice questions and one free-response question. There are no programming questions.

  • You are not allowed to use any notes or access external websites during the exam.

You may drop or withdraw from this course at any time before accessing the final exam. Once you begin the exam, you will be assigned a course grade based on the announced grading formula, and this grade will appear on your university transcript after the eight-week session concludes. After the final exam has ended, you may continue submitting homework assignments until the conclusion of the eight-week session.

Once the "Honor Code Verification" has been submitted, you will no longer be eligible to drop or withdraw from the course, even if you do not access or complete the final assessment.

See the Course Drop & Refund in your program handbook for details.
